clue.text: Cross one river with a note

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Instructions for drawing a map: run one river across another, adding a footnote.
explanation.definitionFit: Cross as an adjective means angry or annoyed, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Rising from the ranks?

parts.note: not promotion of a soldier but an uprising, a rebellion by ordinary people or troops

explanation.surface: A soldier earning promotion from private to officer.
explanation.walkthrough: Rising from the ranks usually means promotion; here a rising is a revolt by the rank and file.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurrection is a violent uprising against authority.

clue.text: Drinks provided in riotous parties

indicators.note: in places the conditional word inside the other letters
riotous means wild and disorderly, so the letters run riot into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
provided, as in on condition that, means if

explanation.surface: Alcohol supplied at wild parties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'provided' reads as supplied, but here means on condition that; 'riotous' is the anagram signal and 'in' the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Aperitifs are alcoholic drinks taken before a meal.

clue.text: The Spanish red rose wine ingredients come from here

parts.note: el is Spanish for the

indicators.note: in a down clue, rose means the word goes upward, so it reads in reverse

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A note that Spanish red and rosé wine use these grapes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rose' looks like rosé wine, but in a down clue it means went up, turning RED into DER.
explanation.definitionFit: Elderberries and elderflowers are made into home-made wines, so the elder tree is their source.

clue.text: One acted in variety show

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: variety suggests a mixed assortment, so the letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A performer once appeared in a variety show on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety' looks like part of the phrase 'variety show', but it is the anagram signal working on I (One), ACTED and IN.
explanation.definitionFit: To show something is to point it out or signal it, a direct synonym as verbs.

clue.text: Act I lines sadly lacking in flexibility

indicators.note: sadly suggests things gone badly wrong, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A drama critic complains the opening act's dialogue is stiff.
explanation.definitionFit: Inelastic materials do not stretch, so they lack flexibility.

clue.text: Get down — from this?

parts.note: down here is the soft fluffy feathers, and the clue asks which bird provides them, while get down also means crouch to avoid something

explanation.surface: An order to take cover, with a question about what to hide from.
explanation.walkthrough: Duck is also the instruction to get down; and down, the soft feathers, comes from ducks (eider especially).
explanation.definitionFit: Ducks supply down feathers, and to duck is to get down quickly.

clue.text: Repeated request for tea dance

indicators.note: repeated says the tea request is said again and again, here three times in all

parts.note: cha (or char) is British slang for tea, so asking for it is simply saying the word
cha is slang for tea, said over and over as an insistent request

explanation.surface: Someone at a tea dance keeps asking for a cuppa.
explanation.walkthrough: Cha is British slang for tea; 'Repeated' has the request made three times over, so the same phrase supplies all three pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The cha-cha-cha is a Latin American ballroom dance.

clue.text: Giant bird on a pole

parts.note: the tit is a small songbird
N stands for north, one of the earth's poles

explanation.surface: A large bird perched on a pole.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titans were the giant gods of Greek myth, so a titan is a giant.

clue.text: Fast moving drug dealers

parts.note: speed is slang for the stimulant amphetamine
merchants are traders or dealers

explanation.surface: Traffickers in narcotics who work quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is slang for people who drive or run very quickly, so it describes those who are fast moving.

clue.text: Policeman gets a lead on forgers — metalworkers!

parts.note: copper is slang for a police officer
smiths are those who work at a forge

explanation.surface: A detective gets a tip-off about counterfeiters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forgers' suggests counterfeiters, but here means those who work metal at a forge; 'gets a lead on' just puts COPPER first.
explanation.definitionFit: Coppersmiths are craftsmen who work in copper, a kind of metalworker.

clue.text: Force to put one means of transport before another

indicators.note: before places the first transport word ahead of the second in the answer

parts.note: rail is travel by train
another means of transport here is the road

explanation.surface: A planner deciding which kind of transport gets priority.
explanation.definitionFit: To railroad someone is the idiom for pushing or forcing them into something hastily.

clue.text: Very occupied by intimate Japanese cult

indicators.note: occupied by means the word for very has the hint word living inside it

parts.note: so means very, as in so good
to intimate is to hint or suggest

explanation.surface: A close-knit Japanese sect with a very busy membership.
explanation.definitionFit: Shinto is the indigenous religion of Japan, loosely called a cult in the sense of a system of worship.

clue.text: It's puzzling how gin and it came to be ordered

indicators.note: being ordered means being put into a new arrangement, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone wonders how a gin and Italian vermouth cocktail ended up being ordered.
explanation.walkthrough: Gin and it is a cocktail of gin and Italian vermouth; here GIN, IT and CAME are the letters rearranged, signalled by 'to be ordered'.
explanation.definitionFit: Enigmatic things are mysterious and baffling, a direct synonym for puzzling.

clue.text: Skinflint having talent for being unhappy

parts.note: a skinflint is a miser who hates spending
having talent means being able or capable

explanation.surface: A gifted tightwad who is nonetheless gloomy.
explanation.definitionFit: Miserable means wretched and very unhappy.

clue.text: One in the club has whip-round for cheese

indicators.note: round means the whip word is placed around the club word

parts.note: the cat-o'-nine-tails is a whip, shortened to cat
one who belongs to a club is a member

explanation.surface: A club member organises a collection to buy some cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'whip-round' looks like a collection of money among club members, but splits into a whip going round. The whip is the cat-o'-nine-tails.
explanation.definitionFit: Camembert is a soft French cheese from Normandy.

clue.text: Murphy's pile?

parts.note: Murphy is slang for a potato, and a heap of potatoes stored under earth and straw has a farming name

explanation.surface: Speculation about the house or fortune of a man named Murphy.
explanation.walkthrough: Murphy is old slang for a potato (from the Irish surname); the answer is a mound of stored potatoes covered with earth, not a stack of anyone's money.
explanation.definitionFit: In farming, a clamp is a heap of potatoes or root vegetables stored under earth and straw.

clue.text: Property charge

definitions.meaning: a property in the sense of a quality or characteristic
to charge something to someone is to ascribe it to them

explanation.definitionFit: As a noun it is a quality or feature; as a verb it means to ascribe or impute.

clue.text: Enquire in the backstreet for jobs

indicators.note: in places the asking word inside the street abbreviation

parts.note: street is ST, and back says read it the other way round
to enquire is to ask

explanation.surface: Asking around in a side street for work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backstreet' reads as one word for a side alley, but splits into the street abbreviation read back, with 'in' as the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasks are pieces of work to be done, a synonym for jobs.

clue.text: Succeed in chase

definitions.meaning: to succeed someone is to follow them in order
to chase someone is to pursue them

explanation.definitionFit: To come after is both to follow in sequence and to pursue someone.

clue.text: Sends away for books

definitions.meaning: to send away for goods is to request them by post
to book a table or seat is to reserve it in advance

explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both requesting goods by mail and reserving or commissioning something.

clue.text: Took the wheel in a Land Rover

indicators.note: in says the letters lie inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Someone drove an off-road vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: Land Rover is a British make of four-wheel-drive vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: To take the wheel is to steer a vehicle, so the past tense of drive.

clue.text: Store memoir up in a novel form

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are given a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bookshop puts an autobiography up for sale reworked as a novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' tempts as literature beside 'memoir', but here means new: MEMOIR and UP are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: An emporium is a large shop selling many kinds of goods, so a store.

clue.text: Waste parts of Cornish river

parts.note: taken as written
the Fal is a river in Cornwall, flowing into the sea at Falmouth

explanation.surface: Rubbish that ends up in a river in Cornwall.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fal is a river in Cornwall, the county at England's south-west tip.
explanation.definitionFit: Offal is the entrails and other parts of a slaughtered animal, originally the waste cut off.

clue.text: The advantage of keenness

definitions.meaning: an ... is a slight advantage, as in having the ...
keenness of a blade is its sharpness

explanation.definitionFit: An edge is both a competitive advantage and the sharpness of a blade.

clue.text: Adam's apple?

parts.note: read literally, the apple that belonged to Adam in Eden, the one he was told not to eat, rather than the throat lump

explanation.surface: A question about the lump in a man's throat.
explanation.walkthrough: The anatomical phrase is reread as the fruit Adam ate in Genesis, which God had banned.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis the fruit of the tree of knowledge was prohibited to Adam and Eve, traditionally pictured as an apple.

clue.text: Frenzied macho types kept in check

indicators.note: kept in means the macho word sits inside the checking word

parts.note: to vet is to check or examine
he-men are macho, muscular types

explanation.surface: Wild tough guys being held under control.
explanation.definitionFit: Vehement means forceful and passionate, close to frenzied in intensity.

clue.text: City editor taken in by the French

indicators.note: taken in by means the editor abbreviation is held inside the French article

parts.note: les is French for the (plural)

explanation.surface: A newspaper's city editor fooled by French people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'City editor' looks like a newspaper job title, but City is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeds is a large city in West Yorkshire, England.
